pages.title: Discrete-time control system and notation (Refresh)
pages.rawText:
Discrete-time control system and notation (Refresh)


   We consider nonlinear, discrete-time systems described by

                                     xt+1 = ft(xt, ut)      t ∈N0                                  (1)

    where xt ∈Rn and ut ∈Rm are the state and the input of the system at time t.


    Notation
   We use x ∈RnT and u ∈RmT to denote, respectively, the stack of the states xt for all t ∈1, . . . , T
    and the inputs ut for all t ∈0, . . . , T −1, that is


                              x := col(x1, . . . , xT )
                             u := col(u0, . . . , uT −1).

    where col(x1, . . . , xT ) is the (column) vector with components x1, . . . , xT .





                                   Prof. Giuseppe Notarstefano – Optimal Control and Reinforcement Learning – Optimality Conditions for Optimal Control 1 |18
pages.text:
Discrete-time control system and notation (Refresh)
We consider nonlinear, discrete-time systems described by
xt+1 = ft(xt, ut) t ∈N0 (1)
where xt ∈Rn and ut ∈Rm are the state and the input of the system at time t.
Notation
We use x ∈RnT and u ∈RmT to denote, respectively, the stack of the states xt for all t ∈1, . . . , T
and the inputs ut for all t ∈0, . . . , T −1, that is
x := col(x1, . . . , xT )
u := col(u0, . . . , uT −1).
where col(x1, . . . , xT ) is the (column) vector with components x1, . . . , xT .

pages.title: System trajectories (Refresh)
pages.rawText:
System trajectories (Refresh)


   We recall the definition of trajectory of a (possibly) nonlinear, discrete-time control system.

     Definition A pair (¯x, ¯u) ∈RnT × RmT  is called a trajectory of system (1) if ¯xt+1 = ft(¯xt, ¯ut) for all
     t ∈0, . . . , T −1. In particular, ¯x is the state trajectory, while ¯u is the input trajectory.        □

    Remark It will be sometimes useful to refer to a generic pair (α, µ) ∈RnT ×RmT with α := col(α1, . . . , αT )
    and µ := col(µ0, . . . , µT −1) as a state-input curve. Notice that a curve (α, µ) is not necessarily a tra-
     jectory, i.e., it does not necessarily satisfy the dynamics (1).                       □





                                   Prof. Giuseppe Notarstefano – Optimal Control and Reinforcement Learning – Optimality Conditions for Optimal Control 2 |18

Unconstrained optimal control problem (discrete-time)


   We look for a solution of the following discrete-time optimal control problem

                                       T −1
                           min X ℓt(xt, ut) + ℓT (xT )                                  (4a)
                           x∈Rn,u∈Rm
                                           t=0
                                      subj.to xt+1 = ft(xt, ut),   t ∈0, . . . , T −1                     (4b)

    with given initial condition x0 = x0 ∈Rn, where ℓt : Rn × Rm →R is the so-called stage cost while
    ℓT  : Rn →R is the terminal cost.


    Remark An optimal control problem constrained only through the dynamics (without boundary and path
     constraints) is named unconstrained optimal control. This notation will be clarified in the following.

    Let (x∗, u∗) be a regular point for the dynamics constraints and an optimal (state-input) trajectory.
    Then there exists λ∗such that ∇L(x∗, u∗, λ∗) = 0.

    Let us explicitly write condition ∇(1,2)L(x∗, u∗, λ∗) = 0

                                             ∇1L(x∗, u∗, λ∗)                              ∇(1,2)L(x∗, u∗, λ∗) =           = 0                                             ∇2L(x∗, u∗, λ∗)
